description: HTTP/2 sessions never clean up if a protocol error is triggered during connection shutdown
overview: An unauthenticated HTTP/2 client can permanently leak Node.js server memory and file descriptors. If a peer triggers a protocol error, for example an oversized frame header, while the session is already shutting down, `nghttp2` tears the session down internally but Node.js never notices, leaving a dangling session: the socket stays in `CLOSE_WAIT` and all of Node.js's HTTP/2 state for that connection is held in memory indefinitely, with no further cost to the attacker. The attacker can start the shutdown remotely by sending `GOAWAY(NO_ERROR)`, so it is reliable against default HTTP/2 servers. It is an incomplete-fix case of CVE-2026-48937: that fix detected `nghttp2` internal terminations by watching for `GOAWAY` sent while not shutting down, but missed terminations that arrive while the session is already shutting down. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
